jobs.title: Product Owner – B2B SaaS (m/w/d)
jobs.description: Über uns CALIMA ist ein Berliner B2B-SaaS-Startup mit der Mission, Arbeitssicherheit durch digitale und innovative Lösungen einfacher, verlässlicher und wirksamer zu machen. Unsere Software unterstützt Unternehmen dabei, dass Alleinarbeitende im Notfall schnell Hilfe erhalten. CALIMA wird von über tausend Unternehmen genutzt und schützt täglich tausende Mitarbeitende. Wir sind ein kleines, ambitioniertes Team mit hohem Qualitätsanspruch. Wir arbeiten pragmatisch, produktnah und mit kurzen Entscheidungswegen. Dabei suchen wir Menschen, die Verantwortung übernehmen, mitdenken und unsere Prozesse aktiv verbessern. Deine Rolle Als Product Owner wirst du unsere erste fest angestellte Person im Produktmanagement und übernimmst die operative Produktverantwortung für unsere Entwicklungsteams: Cloud, Mobile Apps für iOS und Android sowie Platform. Aktuell liegen Backlog, Tickets und Planung direkt beim Head of Tech. Deine Aufgabe ist es, dafür zu sorgen, dass die Teams verlässlich an den richtigen Dingen arbeiten: ein gut sortiertes Backlog, klar definierte Tickets, ein funktionierendes Refinement und realistisch abgestimmte Deadlines. Du wirst das Bindeglied zwischen dem Head of Tech, den kleinen, remote arbeitenden Entwicklungsteams, QA, Sales und Customer Success. Wir entwickeln ein sicherheitsrelevantes Produkt. Zuverlässigkeit und Qualität stehen bei uns vor Feature-Menge. Perspektivisch kannst du deine Rolle in Richtung strategisches Product Management weiterentwickeln und Themen wie Roadmap, Markt und Produktstrategie aktiv mitgestalten. Deine Aufgaben Backlog und Tickets Du übersetzt Anforderungen aus Customer Success, Sales und Support in Epics und Tickets und klärst offene Fragen. Du pflegst ein priorisiertes Backlog je Team und stellst sicher, dass nur klar definierte Tickets in die Entwicklung gehen. jobs.title: Software Developer (gn) @ Autonomous Navigation Venture, Dresden
jobs.description: This is an Atlantic portfolio venture. Find out more about us and other opportunities in our portfolio here . About Soron Systems GPS goes dark. Signals get jammed. Most drones fall out of the sky. Ours don't. Soron Systems is building the navigation brain for autonomous drones that operate where GPS can't be trusted: contested airspace, indoor environments, and GPS denied zones. Born out of cutting edge research at TU Dresden, we've already flown our system under active jamming conditions and proven it works. Now we're going from prototype to product, and we need exceptional engineers to make it happen. This is a rare chance to join at the ground floor of a deep tech startup solving one of the hardest problems in autonomous systems. You'll write code that flies (literally) and see it tested on real hardware within days, not quarters. If you're excited by computer vision, robotics, and building things that matter, keep reading. You'll work directly with the three co-founders, Justus Rischke, Christian Vielhaus, and Johannes Hofer, all from TU Dresden's Deutsche Telekom Chair of Communication Networks. Your Role & Responsibilities You're joining a three-person founding team at the moment that counts - prototype proven, product next. You'll own core parts of the navigation stack from computer vision pipelines to real flight tests. No abstraction layers, no waiting. You write code and watch it fly on hardware you helped build, within days, not quarters. Computer vision: visual inertial odometry, SLAM, and OpenCV pipelines AI object detection and segmentation on NVIDIA Jetson (CUDA) ROS 2 autonomy stack integrated with ArduPilot via MAVLink Embedded Linux deployment with Docker on real UAV platforms and handhelds Simulation in Gazebo and NVIDIA Isaac Sim, plus real flight testing near Dresden What you need to succeed Strong software engineering skills in C++ and Python; comfortable with Git Background in computer science, electrical engineering, robotics, or a related f

More than 75,000 professionals use it every day, accounting for over €100 million ARR across Europe. We’re looking for a Medior AI Engineer to help shape how the intelligent core of that platform evolves. HOW YOU'LL MOVE US FORWARD GenIA-L is a research platform for legal professionals. A user asks a question. The platform searches our trusted sources and turns them into a useful answer. It does this with agents: specialised AI components that each handle part of the question and work together. In the legal domain, an answer can't just sound fluent. It has to be correct, and you must be able to see which source it comes from. This is not a pilot project: the platform runs in production and is used heavily every day. As a medior, your focus is on building. You work independently, on challenges that come from customers and on challenges we spot ourselves. You break down a legal process, translate it into a technical process and work out how to best connect the pieces. Stuck on something? You say so, and your colleagues think along with you. You build and improve the agents of GenIA-L and the way they work together. You build and maintain our knowledge packages: for each legal article, an expert-validated set of commentary, case law, parliamentary history and practical interpretation. You also work on the pipelines that create these packages and keep them up to date. You make quality measurable. jobs.title: Board Test Engineer
jobs.description: About the job Expose manufacturing defects in Graphcore’s advanced circuit boards with tests you build and deploy. Based in Bristol, UK, you’ll develop board and PCBA hardware tests that help turn complex designs into reliable products. You’ll take tests from initial design analysis to deployment, then support them in factories and the field. Better defect coverage means more opportunities to identify manufacturing problems and understand hardware failures when products are in use. You’ll help make test and inspection methods work together, targeting the ways advanced electronic assemblies can go wrong. You’ll examine PCB testability and susceptibility to manufacturing defects, then use that analysis to define and develop test solutions. You’ll build boundary scan and embedded functional tests, turning your understanding of board behaviour into practical diagnostic tools. The team and culture The Product Test and Diagnosis team tackles hardware defects across chips, boards and finished systems. You’ll work directly with Hardware Design, Manufacturing Operations and contract electronics manufacturers, connecting design knowledge with factory experience. Use evidence to guide test decisions, challenge gaps in coverage and take responsibility for moving improvements forward. Move quickly from diagnosis to action, bringing the right people together to resolve hardware problems. What we re looking for Strong electronics fundamentals, particularly digital electronics. Commercial experience in board or PCBA hardware testing. Understanding of manufacturing test for advanced electronic systems. Knowledge of surface-mount technology (SMT), PCB manufacturing processes and their failure mechanisms. Understanding of automated optical inspection (AOI) and automated X-ray inspection (AXI) capabilities. Ability to diagnose electronic defects to component level. jobs.title: Solutions Architect
jobs.description: About Plane Plane's mission is to build the infrastructure the world's work runs on. Every organization runs on three things: the projects it's driving, the knowledge it keeps, and the requests it fields. Plane brings all three into one open, adaptable platform: simple enough for any team to adopt, dependable enough for organizations to build on. And we are building it for a future where humans and AI agents do that work together. Plane began in public on GitHub at the end of 2022. Since then it has grown into a work management platform used by teams around the world: 55,000+ stars, 5,000+ forks, and a contributor community that reads our code and files our issues. Organizations run Plane as a managed Cloud service, on their own infrastructure, or inside fully isolated environments. Building in the open keeps us close to users and raises the standard for everything we ship. Plane is the #1 work infrastructure in aerospace, defense, financial services, and other regulated industries: organizations whose requirements for control, auditability, and data residency rule most software out. When the strictest buyers pick a system of record, that choice means something. Adoption is growing fastest on Plane Cloud and in sovereign clouds, deployments that keep everything inside a country's own borders and rules. Plane is backed by top investors and built across San Francisco, London, and Hyderabad. We work in tightly knit teams, stay close to users, and care about the visible product as much as the unglamorous details that make software dependable. People own problems end to end, and we add process only when it helps the work. Humans and agents We believe the next decade of work will be done by humans and AI agents together. Not agents replacing people, and not a chat window bolted onto software built for humans clicking around, but both working in one system of action, where an agent's work is as visible and as accountable as a person's. Most software treats AI as a feature.

jobs.title: Embedded Software Engineer
jobs.description: De uitdaging Onze klant ontwikkelt high-tech embedded systemen die extreem betrouwbaar, veilig en performant moeten zijn. Je werkt in een omgeving waar innovatie de standaard is en waar jouw code direct invloed heeft op hardware, sensoren, controllers en real-time verwerking. We zoeken engineers die met plezier de diepte ingaan: van low-level drivers tot robust architecture en van integratie tot performance-optimalisatie. Wat ga je doen? Als Embedded Software Engineer werk je via GradeMatch binnen een multidisciplinair engineeringteam dat software, elektronica en systeemarchitectuur combineert. Je ontwikkelt embedded software in C en C++, analyseert hardware-interactie, werkt met RTOS-omgevingen en draagt bij aan nieuwe en bestaande modules. Je krijgt te maken met complexe systemen, nieuwe productfeatures, protocollen, edge computing, testscenario’s en integratie met high-end apparatuur. Hoe je impact maakt Je implementeert embedded softwaremodules in C en C++ volgens hoge kwaliteitseisen en werkt aan drivers, interfaces, communicatiestromen en configuratiecomponenten. Je stelt duidelijke requirements op en denkt actief mee over designkeuzes, terwijl je samen met andere engineers high-level en low-level architectuurvoorstellen uitwerkt. Daarnaast test en review je code op betrouwbaarheid, performance en stabiliteit en werk je nauw samen met hardware engineers om een correcte integratie te waarborgen. Je begeleidt de live-gang, validatie en nazorg binnen de embedded omgeving en documenteert code, flows, architectuur en testresultaten zorgvuldig. Wat je van ons krijgt Salaris: €3.500 - €6.000 bruto per maand, afhankelijk van ervaring Uitdagende projecten bij een high-tech klant via GradeMatch Opleidingen, begeleiding en technische sparringpartners Hybride werken mogelijk Mogelijkheden tot specialisatie (RTOS, C++, architectuur, security, Linux internals) Wat het jou oplevert Werken aan cutting-edge embedded technologie binnen een high-tech organisatie. jobs.description: Senior AI/ML Engineer, remote in Canada: own the AI that assesses patients for US healthcare providers and gets them to the right mental health care faster. About Limbic Limbic’s vision is to ensure the highest quality therapy is accessible to everyone, everywhere. Limbic has supported more than 820,000 patients across the UK and the US. We are used in over 50% of NHS Talking Therapies services, which makes us the largest-ever deployment of generative AI for direct patient care, and our AI now delivers end-to-end therapy to patients in the US under the supervision of licensed clinicians. Safety and science come first. We are the only AI mental health chatbot with UKCA Class IIa medical device certification, and the first AI-led mental healthcare company selected for the FDA’s TEMPO pilot. Our results are published in leading scientific journals: in a randomized, double-blind trial published in Nature Medicine, our AI agents scored higher than licensed CBT therapists on a standard measure of therapy skill. jobs.title: Software Engineer, AI Coding Tasks
jobs.description: We're looking for experienced software engineers to build AI coding tasks from a codebase they know well. US$1,000 per task, and you can do as many tasks as you want. You turn a real change from a repository you know into a task that today's best AI coding models struggle with: hard for the models, but fair for a skilled engineer. Your tasks are used to measure and train AI coding models. Remote, any location. US$1,000 per task that passes review. Minimum of one task a week, about 10 hours a week. How it works Apply. Complete a short screener interview and upload your resume. Propose. Once you're selected, pick a change from a repository you know and submit a short proposal. We approve it or suggest a better candidate. Build. In our platform, set up the repository as it was before the change, then write the brief, the correct solution and the grading checks. Stress-test. Try lazy, incorrect and shortcut solutions and make sure your checks catch them. Model testing. Run your task against leading AI models until strong models often fail but a skilled engineer can clearly solve it. Review. A reviewer checks your task and you revise it. Most tasks take more than one round. Next task. Once your task is accepted, start another. Requirements 2+ years of professional software engineering Code merged into a public open-source repository, ideally one you know well. A private codebase you own may also qualify (not employer or client code) Strong in at least one of Python, TypeScript, Go, Rust, Java or C++ Solid with Docker, Linux, Git and automated testing Regular use of an AI coding tool Experience writing tests, rubrics or evaluation criteria, ideally for AI models You can explain a change clearly and concisely, in your own words At least 10 hours a week, starting now A secure personal or work computer (no public or shared machines) Nice to have Deep expertise in one area, such as databases, compilers, distributed systems, security or infrastructure Experience building agent
